references.text: The parallel passage in [ref:Matt 24:50-51|Matthew 24:50-51] is almost identical to Luke 12:46. Here the expression is also used that the Lord will come on a day when the servant does not expect him and at an hour he does not know, and that he will cut him in pieces and assign him a place with the hypocrites.
[ref:1 Tess 5:2-3|1 Thessalonians 5:2-3] speaks of the Lord's day coming like a thief in the night, unexpectedly – the same motif of unexpected arrival as in Luke 12:46.
[ref:2 Pet 3:10|2 Peter 3:10] describes how the Lord's day will come like a thief and emphasizes the unexpected arrival just as Luke 12:46 does.
[ref:Åp 3:3|Revelation 3:3] warns that the Lord will come like a thief if the church does not keep watch – the same motif of unexpected judgment as in Luke 12:46.
[ref:Luk 12:39-40|Luke 12:39-40] is the immediate context where Jesus has already used the image of the thief coming unexpectedly, which prepares for the climax of the warning in verse 46.
[ref:Matt 25:30|Matthew 25:30] describes the fate of the unprofitable servant: to be cast out into outer darkness. This is a parallel picture of judgment on the unfaithful servant, as in Luke 12:46.

[ref:Hebr 10:26-27|Hebrews 10:26-27] warns that for those who sin willfully after receiving the truth, there remains only a fearful judgment – this corresponds with the severe judgment on the unfaithful servant in Luke 12:46.
[ref:Matt 24:42-44|Matthew 24:42-44] exhorts to watchfulness because the Lord will come at an hour one does not expect, the same motif that underlies the judgment in Luke 12:46.

[ref:Luk 21:34-36|Luke 21:34-36] warns that that day will come unexpectedly upon those who are occupied with the things of this world – something that mirrors the fate of the unfaithful servant in Luke 12:46.
[ref:Åp 16:15|Revelation 16:15] repeats Jesus' words that he will come like a thief, and blessed is the one who keeps watch – an echo of the warning about unexpected judgment in Luke 12:46.
